notes:
Missouri has no recurring franchise-type levy on a default LLC: applies is false. The corporation franchise tax of chapter 147, RSMo is ended by its own text: subsection (5) of section 147.010 states that for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2016, no annual franchise tax shall be imposed. Even while it existed it was a corporation levy, so it never reached a default LLC; the Department's small-business page says a partnership-taxed LLC generally pays no income tax and its income passes directly through to members. One stale signal is worth recording: several Department of Revenue pages still carry a shared meta description naming "corporation franchise tax" among the taxes the Department collects, but the statute is the newer and authoritative statement, and the recorded value follows the statute.
collectedWithAnnualReport is null: no franchise-type levy exists, and root states.json carries annual_report_fee 0 for Missouri, which has no annual report requirement for LLCs.
stateIncomeTax: members of a partnership-taxed LLC report the passed-through income on their Missouri individual returns. The top individual rate for tax year 2025 is 4.7%, per the Department's capital-gains FAQ, and the 2025 rate schedule tops out at 4.70%.
hasPTETElection is true: the SALT Parity Act (Section 143.436, RSMo) lets a partnership or S corporation annually elect to become an affected business entity paying the pass-through entity tax, effective for tax years ending on or after December 31, 2022; the statutory definition quoted in the Department's FAQ includes a limited liability company treated as a partnership, and the election's rate is the highest individual rate.
